items.text: The tradition of sending greeting cards has withstood the rise of digital communication.

level1.label: 主语
level1.text: The tradition of sending greeting cards

items.text: Though often inexpensive, cards can convey our thoughts and emotions.
Their rich history spreads over centuries of civilisations across the world, building a culture of card giving along its way.

level1.label: 状语
level1.text: building a culture of card giving along its way

items.text: It was written in a 2011 edition of Souvenirs, Gifts, & Novelties that since the earliest days of written interaction, special occasions such as birthdays and seasonal celebrations have been recognised through handwritten notes and letters.

level1.label: 主语从句
level1.text: that since the earliest days of written interaction, special occasions such as birthdays and seasonal celebrations have been recognised through handwritten notes and letters

items.text: Ancient Egyptians wrote scrolls.
In China, wishes of good fortune were sent in decorative red envelopes around Chinese New Year.
And similarly, cards featuring classical Persian poetic verse written in calligraphy were exchanged.

level1.label: 主语
level1.text: cards featuring classical Persian poetic verse written in calligraphy

level2.label: 后置定语
level2.text: featuring classical Persian poetic verse written in calligraphy

items.text: These gestures paved the way for the culture of greeting cards.
Before the printing revolution of the 15th century, only those with lots of money would write cards.

level1.label: 主语
level1.text: only those with lots of money

items.text: Since then, they have become more accessible, meaning more people could communicate from a distance.

level1.label: 状语
level1.text: meaning more people could communicate from a distance

level2.label: 宾语从句
level2.text: more people could communicate from a distance

items.text: As industrialisation continued to sweep through the 19th century, sending cards became a widespread practice.

level1.label: 时间状语从句
level1.text: As industrialisation continued to sweep through the 19th century

items.text: During the Victorian period, greeting cards became quite elaborate in design.
They were adorned with lace, ribbon, and intricate illustrations.
The cards themselves became keepsakes, treasured for their beauty and sentiment.

level1.label: 表语
level1.text: keepsakes, treasured for their beauty and sentiment

level2.label: 后置定语
level2.text: treasured for their beauty and sentiment

items.text: Nowadays, we see a variety of designs.
Most cards still leave a blank space inside for a handwritten message.
Some cards can even be designed online to include pictures of loved ones, adding a more personal touch.

level1.label: 状语
level1.text: to include pictures of loved ones

items.text: According to Ken Research, from 2024 the global greeting card market was valued at around $19 billion.
With that, and increasing concerns about the environment, many manufacturers are changing how they make their cards.
They're using recycled and other environmentally friendly materials, like biodegradable glitter and paper made from sustainable plant fibres like bamboo.

level1.label: 宾语
level1.text: recycled and other environmentally friendly materials, like biodegradable glitter and paper made from sustainable plant fibres like bamboo

level2.label: 后置定语
level2.text: made from sustainable plant fibres like bamboo

items.text: So, we can continue our kind tradition of card giving without harming the planet.

level1.label: 宾语
level1.text: our kind tradition of card giving
